title: Halting Characterisation of the Final Scan
statement: Let $K_0,B,P,j$ be natural numbers, let $x$ be a Boolean word, let $\mathcal O$ assign a Boolean answer to each of four indices and each Boolean word, let $S=(N,L_g,s,s_1,X,w,K,B_s,U,V,T,T_2,Z,C,ch,c,c_1)$ be a machine state, and let $M:\mathbb Z\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ be a memory marking. Suppose $K-U=j$ using truncated subtraction, $U\le K$, $T=T_2=Z=0$, every coordinate of $S$ is at most $B$, $B_s+K\le B$, $B_s+K\le P$, and $K+1\le B$. Then the machine started in its final-scan state with registers given by $S$, memory $M$, and memory head at $0$ halts while its guard holds at every time strictly before halting. Its answer is true exactly when there exists $v\in\mathbb N$ such that $U\le v<K$, $M(B_s+v)=\mathrm{true}$, and $\mathcal O$ at index $3$ answers true on the encoding of $x$ paired with the encodings of $v$ and $s$.
hypotheses_covered: An oracle on four indices and Boolean words
A machine state $S$ and memory marking $M$
Every coordinate of $S$ is at most $B$
replaced:
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $x$
be a Boolean word, and let $K_0,B,P,j$ be natural numbers, with an oracle assigning a
Boolean answer to each of four indices and each Boolean word. Let $S$ be a machine state
and $M:\mathbb Z\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ a memory marking. Suppose $j=K-U$,
$U\le K$, the two walk counters and scratch register are zero, every register of $S$ is
at most $B$, $B_s+K\le B$, $B_s+K\le P$, and $K+1\le B$. Then the machine started in its
final-scan state with registers given by $S$, memory $M$, and memory head at $0$ halts
while satisfying the following guard at every time before halting: every register is at
most $B$, the current instruction's required safety condition holds, and the memory head
lies between $0$ and $P$. Its Boolean answer is true exactly when there exists a natural
number $v$ with $U\le v<K$, $M(B_s+v)=\mathrm{true}$, and the oracle at index $3$
answers true on the encoding of $x$ paired with the encodings of $v$ and $s$.
